messages:
liam (customer): Hey team — our rerank calls started failing after we increased candidate set. We hit a 413 / "Payload Too Large" from the rerank endpoint. Previously 100 docs worked, now 500 fails. Example minimal repro (we're truncating docs here):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": "Explain async I/O in node.js (very long query...)", "documents": ["<very long doc 1>", "<very long doc 2>", ..., "<very long doc 500>"] }'
```

The gateway returns: `\{"error":"request entity too large", "code":413, "message":"payload exceeds 1048576 bytes"\}`. This blocks our batch rerank latency SLO (need <300ms end-to-end). Any ideas? :grimacing:

maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for the repro. A couple quick asks so we can triage: 1) can you paste the exact error payload and the raw request size if available? 2) average size of each doc (chars) and whether docs are HTML/markdown/JSON. 3) are you using hosted API or Dedicated?

liam (customer): Hosted API. Docs are mostly JSON blobs (base64 images removed) and average ~3KB each. With 500 docs that's ~1.5MB payload which matches the error. Error response body: ```{"error":"request entity too large","code":413,"details":"client_max_body_size exceeded"}```. We definitely need to rerank 500 candidates in a single call ideally — splitting hurts latency.

maya (support): Thanks — that makes sense. Two possible classes of fixes: a) short-term workarounds (split into N smaller rerank calls, or do a pre-filter step with embeddings) and b) product/infra fixes (increase client_max_body_size or surface a clearer API error with actionable guidance). I'll escalate.

jorge (eng-runtime): FYI the 413 and "client_max_body_size" look like nginx/gateway rejecting before request hits the rerank service. That's an infra-level limit (default 1MB in some proxies) not an LLM token limit. We shouldn't silently fail later with model errors. Suggested steps: 1) confirm the exact raw bytes in the failing request logs (liam, if you can paste the Content-Length header value that helps), 2) short-term we can add a server-side pre-check that returns a clearer 400 with a helpful message like: "Rerank request exceeds payload limit (payload N bytes > allowed M). Try reducing number of documents or truncating documents; consider prefiltering with embeddings. Docs: <link>".

liam (customer): Content-Length was 1624321. Ok good to know it's gateway-body-size, not token count. But increasing max body size would just move the pain down the chain (model token limits, memory). Are there recommended patterns for us to keep single-request rerank semantics?

zoe (eng-ml): Two recommended production patterns we use for customers: 1) Embedding + ANN prefilter: compute dense embeddings for each doc, run ANN to pluck top ~100 candidates, then call rerank on that smaller set. This keeps one network hop to the embedding store + a single small rerank call. 2) Progressive batching: keep batch size small (e.g., 100) and do parallel rerank calls with deterministic merging. Both preserve quality and are more resilient to proxy limits. Pseudocode for pattern 1:

```python
# prefilter pipeline (sketch)
query_emb = embed(query)
candidates = ann_index.search(query_emb, k=1000)  # fast, cheap
top_prefilter = candidates[:150]
rerank_payload = {"query": query_text, "documents": [d.text for d in top_prefilter]}
resp = requests.post('/v1/rerank', json=rerank_payload)
```

This reduces payload by ~80-90% in your numbers. If you absolutely must do 500, consider compressing documents client-side (gzip) and stream; but hosted API may not accept gzip for JSON bodies today.

billing-bot: Quick billing note: we bill on successful inference tokens consumed. If the request fails at the gateway (413) and doesn't reach inference, there should be no model-token charge for that call. If you're seeing charges on failures please file a billing ticket with request ids.

maya (support): Action items I'm taking: 1) I'll send liam a short troubleshooting doc with a sample prefilter + batching script and a trimmed payload that should succeed. 2) I'll open an infra ticket to consider raising the proxy limit for Hosted (short-term) but we need a long-term rate/size policy. 3) Asking eng to add a better error message for oversized rerank bodies.

jorge (eng-runtime): Filed GH#4567 for a two-part fix: (A) return a 400 with a structured error when the gateway rejects body size with guidance and estimated limits, (B) add server-side token/payload pre-check to return `error_type: input_too_large` with fields: `max_bytes`, `actual_bytes`, `suggested_actions` (truncate_docs, use_prefilter). I'll link the patch once it's up.

zoe (eng-ml): I'll add a cookbook snippet to the dev docs showing the embedding-prefilter + rerank flow and a sample script for pairwise merging results.

liam (customer): Thanks — the prefilter approach should work and we'll try parallel rerank with top-100. Please ping me when the clearer error is live so we can remove the temporary client-side guard. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

maya (support): Will do — assigning follow-ups: triage doc -> maya; infra ticket -> jorge; docs snippet -> zoe. Closing loop here once GH#4567 lands.
